title: Accurate I/O Jitter Estimation by Fractional-Exponent Q-Scale Polynomial
content: Accurate estimation of total jitter (TJ) at low bit error rates (BERs) is essential for high-speed serial interfaces, where direct measurement is often impractical. The dual-Dirac model is widely used due to its simplicity and linear TJ-Q relationship, but its assumption that deterministic jitter (DJ) consists of two Dirac impulses does not capture practical jitter distributions. Simulations show that this linear TJ-Q prediction can introduce significant errors. Prior work using higher-order polynomial fitting improves accuracy but depends strongly on input data range selection. This work investigates the impact of DJ distributions on TJ-Q behavior through a convolution-based numerical jitter simulation framework. A fractional-exponent Q-scale polynomial model is proposed to better align with physical nature of the jitter distribution, improve low-BER jitter prediction accuracy while maintaining similar computational complexity. Results show that, with measurements down to 10⁻⁶ BER, the proposed method predicts jitter at 10−12 BER with over 90% error reduction (10× accuracy improvement) over the linear method and 60–80%+ improvement over fourth-order polynomial fitting. Measurements down to 10−9 BER further enable prediction at 10⁻²⁰ and 10⁻²⁷ BER levels with excellent accuracy, extending extrapolation by up to 18 orders of magnitude.
